parts.description:
Functional Description

Bicistronic sensing module: Drosophila melanogaster odorant receptor Or19a (387 aa), an EMCV internal ribosome entry site, and mCherry, with a GCCACC Kozak. Needs promoter and polyA from the host vector.

One transcript gives two separate proteins: Or19a is translated cap-dependently, mCherry from the IRES as an independent expression marker. Downstream expression is expected to be lower than the upstream cistron - acceptable for a bright constitutive marker.

Or19a is expected to assemble with Orco into a heteromeric ligand-gated ion channel; odorant binding opens the channel and admits extracellular Ca2+. This part does not report the signal itself - a co-expressed Orco module with a calcium indicator is required.

Red fluorescence confirms the transcript is present, not receptor folding or trafficking; no epitope tag is included.

Caution: no odorant-specific response was reported in a published HEK293 panel, despite a VUAA1 response (Zboray 2023).

parts.description:
Functional Description

Encodes a 35-aa N-terminal leader from the pRSET vector series: a His6 tag, T7 gene-10 tag, and Xpress epitope with an enterokinase site.

 

In mammalian cells this leader is functionally inert - it targets the protein nowhere and is not cleaved. Its value is as a detection handle: a fusion protein carrying no other epitope tag can be detected by anti-His or anti-Xpress antibody and its full length confirmed by western blot.

 

Carries its own ATG but no stop codon; intended for the 5' end of a fusion ORF. It can be omitted without affecting downstream domains.

 

Source: pRSET series (Invitrogen). Present here because it is carried by the parent GCaMP6f plasmid pGP-CMV-GCaMP6f (Addgene #40755).

Functional Description

Encodes the Drosophila melanogaster tuning odorant receptor Or67b, codon-optimized for human expression.

Insect ORs are not GPCRs. Or67b is expected to assemble with the co-receptor Orco into a heteromeric ligand-gated ion channel, in which Or67b provides ligand specificity and Orco forms the pore. parts.description:
Functional Description

Single-ORF translational fusion of the calcium indicator GCaMP6f to the N-terminus of Drosophila melanogaster Orco, joined by a flexible (GGGGS)3 linker, with an RSET leader and a GCCACC Kozak. Needs promoter and polyA from the host vector.

Orco assembles with a co-expressed tuning odorant receptor to form a heteromeric ligand-gated ion channel. Odorant binding opens the channel, extracellular Ca2+ enters, and the fused GCaMP6f brightens (ex ~485, em ~535 nm).

GCaMP6f is N-terminal because Orco has inverted topology with an intracellular N-terminus; a C-terminal fusion would strand the indicator outside the cell, where millimolar Ca2+ saturates it. The fusion gives 1:1 indicator-to-receptor stoichiometry and holds the sensor at the channel mouth.

Expected to respond to the Orco agonist VUAA1 alone; odorant responses need a co-expressed tuning receptor. Signal depends entirely on extracellular Ca2+.

parts.description:
Functional Description

Encodes a 15-aa flexible glycine-serine linker, (GGGGS)x3, for joining two domains in a translational fusion. Glycine gives backbone flexibility, serine keeps it hydrophilic; the sequence forms no secondary structure and has no protease-sensitive motifs.

 

The length lets each domain fold and move independently while keeping them close. This matters when one domain senses a signal generated by the other - e.g. a calcium indicator fused to an ion channel, where a longer tether would move the indicator out of the steep Ca2+ microdomain at the pore, and a shorter one would constrain the conformational change that generates the signal.

 

The three repeats use diversified synonymous codons so the DNA contains no tandem repeat - a common cause of synthesis failure. Request codon diversification explicitly when ordering any (GGGGS)n linker.

 

No start or stop codon; place in frame between two coding domains.

parts.description:
Functional Description

Encodes the Drosophila melanogaster olfactory co-receptor Orco (486 aa), codon-optimised for human expression.

 

Orco is the universal co-receptor of insect olfaction. It binds no odorant itself, but forms a heteromeric ligand-gated ion channel with any tuning odorant receptor and chaperones that receptor to the plasma membrane. Because the complex is a channel and not a GPCR, no extra signal-transduction machinery is needed in a heterologous host: odorant binding opens the channel directly, admitting extracellular Ca2+.

 

Orco has inverted topology relative to GPCRs (intracellular N-terminus), so a cytosolic sensor domain must be fused at the N-terminus. The channel is expected to open to the synthetic agonist VUAA1 independently of any odorant, making VUAA1 a convenient positive control.

 

Includes a stop codon but no start context. Reference: FlyBase FBgn0037324 | FBtr0078794 | RefSeq NP_524235. Protein identical to the FlyBase reference (486 aa).

parts.description:
Functional Description

Encodes GCaMP6f, a genetically encoded calcium indicator: RS20/M13 peptide from myosin light-chain kinase, a circularly permuted EGFP, and calmodulin. Ca2+ binding to calmodulin drives a conformational change that increases fluorescence (ex ~485 nm, em ~535 nm).

 

GCaMP6f is weakly fluorescent at resting Ca2+ and brightens on binding, so low green fluorescence in unstimulated cells is expected and is not a sign of failed expression. The fluorophore is pH-sensitive: buffers used outside a CO2 incubator should be pH-stabilised with HEPES, or baseline drift can be mistaken for signal.

 

Contains no start or stop codon. Intended as an internal domain of a fusion protein; requires an in-frame ATG, promoter and polyA from the host vector.

 

Source: pGP-CMV-GCaMP6f (Addgene #40755, RRID:Addgene_40755), gift of Douglas Kim & GENIE Project. Chen et al. 2013, Nature 499:295, doi:10.1038/nature12354.
